text:
Oxford County placed 7th among Maine counties for Housing Choice Vouchers assisted units in 2025
R. P. Boyer
Oxford County placed 7th among 16 Maine counties in the 2025 Housing Choice Vouchers assisted-unit ranking, with 563 assisted units.
Assisted units in Oxford County rose from 553 in 2024, an increase of 10 units.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally reduce rent for low-income households that meet program eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households describes three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Public housing is owned by local housing agencies, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households lease homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance typically pay rent equal to 30% of their income after deductions, with the federal government covering the remainder. Eligibility depends on HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are generally placed on a waiting list until assistance is available.
